saints.name: St. Mark
saints.title: Evangelist
saints.shortBlurb: The evangelist whose brief, vivid Gospel preserves the preaching of St. Peter, and traditional founder of the Church of Alexandria…
biography: Mark, the John Mark of the Acts of the Apostles, was the son of Mary, in whose Jerusalem house the first Christians gathered to pray, and a cousin of Barnabas. He accompanied Paul and Barnabas as an assistant on their first journey but turned back at Perga, a failing that later drove the two apostles apart.

Reconciled to Paul, he is found beside the apostle during the Roman imprisonment, and Peter greets the churches with 'Mark my son'. Papias, early in the second century, records that Mark became Peter's interpreter and wrote down accurately, though not in order, the apostle's preaching — the shortest of the four Gospels.

Ancient tradition sends him to Egypt as founder and first bishop of the Church of Alexandria, where, his later Acts relate, he was martyred, dragged through the streets, about the year 68. In 828 Venetian merchants bore his relics from Alexandria to Venice, whose patron he became; the winged lion of the evangelist is her emblem still.
saints.knownFor: Writing the Gospel that preserves Peter's preaching.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 25 April
